tagline: Cross-border clean commuting on Western Europe's largest alpine lake.
summary: Lake Geneva (Lac Léman) links Geneva, Lausanne, Montreux and the French shore with one of Europe's most established lake-transport networks, exceptional affluence and strict environmental rigour — an unusually ready market for silent, zero-emission foiling.

use_cases.title: Cross-lake commuting
use_cases.body: A fast Geneva↔Lausanne (~30 nm) foiling commute between the two largest cities.

use_cases.title: Cross-border hops
use_cases.body: Silent zero-wake Geneva↔Évian/Thonon (~5 nm) links to the French shore.

use_cases.title: Montreux Riviera links
use_cases.body: Premium Lausanne↔Montreux (~12 nm) runs along the Lavaux vineyards.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: All Léman corridors (Geneva↔Lausanne ~30 nm, cross-border Évian ~5 nm, Riviera ~12 nm) sit inside the all-electric envelope over flat alpine water; near-silent zero-wake operation suits the lake's strict environmental rules. Quanta-LR is not required.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required on the lake; all corridors are well inside the all-electric envelope.

competitive_landscape: Today: the diesel/hybrid CGN cross-border fleet and lakeside roads. The pain is slow crossings and a congested shoreline under strict emissions rules — the status quo a faster, cleaner tier improves on.
seasonality: Year-round operation; alpine lake conditions are calm and sheltered, ideal for foiling in all seasons.
regulatory_note: Switzerland and France jointly regulate Léman with strict environmental and wake controls; Switzerland's stringent emissions standards and established electric-boat culture make zero-emission foiling an excellent fit, with CGN providing a public cross-border model.
